cross_references.relationship: Section 835a governs the force used during an arrest; section 836 governs the authority to make the arrest in the first place. Force analysis presupposes arrest authority.
DV response under section 13701 may require arrest of the dominant aggressor; any force used during that arrest is governed by section 835a.
Companion bill requiring every agency to adopt a use-of-force policy consistent with section 835a by January 1, 2021.
Federal 'objective reasonableness' standard for Fourth Amendment excessive force claims. Section 835a intentionally exceeds Graham by requiring necessity, not just reasonableness.

Excessive force by state officers is actionable under section 1983 as a Fourth Amendment violation. California's section 835a provides a higher standard that may inform the reasonableness analysis in federal claims.
Bane Act — use of force that interferes with constitutional rights through threats, intimidation, or coercion is actionable under the Bane Act as a state civil rights claim.
